Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star one to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield Technologies' results for the Q3 2024. With me on today's call are Sarah Kline, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer, and Raj Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Kline.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberShield had an exceptional Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: strengthening our market position through consistent share gains, elevating competitive win rates in head-to-head battles, optimizing channel partner contributions for scalable growth, expanding our base of high-value customers with substantial ARR, and grounding our outlook in disciplined guidance assumptions.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah highlighted, we had a remarkable Q3. Revenue reached $312 million, reflecting a 28% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $215 million, and net income was $48 million, translating to $0.72 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year based on these outstanding results.

To give you deeper context on our momentum, let me start with market share trends, which continue to underscore CyberShield's leadership in the cybersecurity landscape. The global cybersecurity market is projected by Gartner to hit $212 billion in 2024, up 14% year-over-year, propelled by ransomware attacks that surged 37% in the first half according to Chainalysis, faster cloud migrations, and the rise of GenAI-enabled threats. Our addressable market in endpoint detection and response, extended detection and response, and secure access service edge solutions comes to about $85 billion.

The top line here: CyberShield's global market share in the EDR/XDR category climbed from 14.2% at the end of Q3 2023 to 17.8% as of Q3 2024, based on IDC's latest Worldwide Semiannual Endpoint Security Tracker. That's our third straight quarter of sequential gains, beating the category's 22% YoY growth. In SASE, we've moved from 9.1% to 12.4% share per Forrester's Wave report, thanks to our ShieldEdge platform's zero-trust convergence features. Across our unified portfolio, we've grabbed 2.3 points of share year-to-date, equating to around $1.2 billion in added annual revenue at today's pricing.

Zooming into segments, our ShieldXDR platform shone brightly, posting 28% YoY bookings growth and taking 1.8 points from legacy players like Symantec Endpoint Protection and even nibbling at CrowdStrike's Falcon dominance. We've had real pull in mid-market enterprises, where our AI-native behavioral analytics via the NeuroThreat engine cut false positives by 45% below industry averages, confirmed by MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. This plays perfectly into the consolidation trend, with CISOs ditching point solutions—our single-pane-of-glass XDR now makes up 62% of new customer logos, versus 48% last year.

By region, North America, 52% of our revenue and 58% of the global EDR market, we maintained 22.4% share—our best region—with a 0.9-point YoY gain despite pressure from Palo Alto's Cortex XDR. Highlights include a $150 million multi-year deal with a top-5 U.S. bank switching from Microsoft Defender, praising our ransomware rollback through immutable backups tied to ShieldXDR. Hyperscaler pricing has softened ASPs by 3% in NA, but we're pushing back with value pricing linked to MTTR SLAs, now in 70% of deals.

EMEA has been our hottest spot, with share jumping from 11.2% to 15.6%, a 4.4-point leap, thanks to GDPR enforcement and threats from groups like APT28. Our EBA-compliant data sovereignty in Frankfurt and Dublin data centers fueled 35% YoY ACV growth, including a pan-European telco rollout that bumped Zscaler's ZPA from SSE, citing ShieldEdge's 99.999% uptime and 40% latency cuts for remote teams via SD-WAN.

In APAC, 22% of revenue, share rose from 8.7% to 11.9%, riding digital shifts in Japan, India, and Southeast Asia. Regulations like India's DPDP Act and Singapore's cybersecurity code spurred demand; Q3 APAC bookings rose 41% YoY, with ShieldXDR in 25% of new Fortune 1000 setups. Local rivals like Trend Micro pose challenges, but ties with Tencent Cloud for hybrid protection added 150,000 endpoints in China.

LatAm and Middle East/Africa, combining for 10% of revenue, saw share grow from 4.1% to 6.8%. Our ShieldIoT agent for IoT/OT has caught on amid supply chain hits echoing SolarWinds.

These moves affirm our Unified Threat Fabric launched at RSAC 2024, blending EDR, NDR, and CWPP in a fabric-agnostic setup. YTD R&D spend of $250 million includes quantum-resistant crypto pilots with NIST post-quantum algorithms, prepping for the 2025 shift. We're outpacing EDR pure-plays like SentinelOne, whose share dipped 1.2 points, by bundling SASE, and our 95% gross retention beats the industry's 88%.

For FY24, we see EDR/XDR share ending at 18.5%, with Q4 adding another 0.7 points. Watch for macro IT budget squeezes of 5-7% per Deloitte and AI malware evolution from LockBit. Our counters: ShieldGenAI beta for 500 adopters in adversary emulation, and M&A in deception tech to lift our 30% NDR share.

In short, we're not just growing—we're defining the market.

Shifting to another key metric, our competitive win rates, which track the percentage of deals where we displace incumbents or prevail in bake-offs for new logos. This is vital in cybersecurity, with threats like LockBit RaaS and nation-states pushing TAM growth to 12-15% CAGR through 2028 per Gartner and IDC.

In Q3, overall win rates hit 44.2%, up 620 basis points YoY from 38% and 210 bps from Q2's 42.1%—our best in three years. Trailing 12-month at 42.8%, this supports our $2.1 billion ARR.

By portfolio, XDR wins reached 51%, up from 43% YoY, as ForgeXDR—wait, ShieldXDR—beats Falcon and Defender with 28% fewer false positives per AV-TEST, plus 40% faster MTTR via SIEM ties to Splunk and Elastic. SASE hit 47%, displacing Zscaler Zero Trust in 62% of cases with sub-50ms latency on AWS Outposts and Azure Stack. Legacy EDR was 36% against SentinelOne, but 75% upsell to full XDR lifts ACV 22% to $1.2 million.

Regionally, NA at 48%, fueled by CMMC 2.0; a $150 million win over Prisma Cloud at a top defense firm. EMEA 43%, up 800 bps on NIS2; 55% vs. Check Point in finance with quantum-resistant DORA encryption. APAC 39%, up 1,100 bps via Alibaba and Tencent bundles, netting $200 million TCV from telcos and banks against Salt Typhoon.

Vertically, finance 52% over Fortinet NGFW, healthcare 46% post-Change Healthcare, manufacturing 38% in OT/IoT vs. Nozomi, public sector 35% with 28% win-backs from McAfee.

Drivers: Technical edge from $450 million R&D in ShieldAI copilot for autonomous hunting, cutting burnout 35%, securing LLMs vs. prompt injection—key in 70% wins. Sales evolution with 92% gross retention, 128% NRR, 65% multi-product wins at 3.2 modules. Ecosystem co-sells with Snowflake and ServiceNow edged 42% of pursuits.

Vs. Big Four (Palo Alto, CrowdStrike, Zscaler, Fortinet) at 39%, 58% vs. Tier 2 like Symantec/McAfee, with 1,200-seat migrations. Gaining in $45 billion SASE growing 25% in 2025 via converged stacks.

Q4 win rates eyed at 43-45%, upside from ShieldQuantum PQC suite with NIST ML-KEM/ML-DSA. Risks: longer cycles, pricing wars, offset by 75% expansion wins. This sets us for 20%+ growth in 2025.

Next, on channel partner performance, a core growth engine. Our ecosystem—VARs, MSPs, SIs, distributors like Ingram Micro, TD Synnex, Arrow—scales our Zero Trust platform, ShieldXDR, CNAPP, SSPM.

Q3 channels delivered $194 million, 62% of $312 million total, up 12% sequentially and 27% YoY, topping our 28% overall growth amid 35% ransomware surge and Change Healthcare fallout.

By type: Distributors 38% or $74 million, up 18% YoY via hyperscaler marketplaces, 40% XDR attach to AWS. VARs/SIs 45% or $87 million, up 32%, with CDW/SHI/Presidio at $450K ACV on NDR-Prisma POCs. MSPs 17% or $33 million, up 45%, bundling AI threat hunting with RMM, 85% renewals, 28% ARR expansion.

Top 10 partners 48% share via 22% rebates, $1.2 million co-op funds.

Regions: Americas 55% ($107 million, +24% YoY) on CISA zero-trust, WWT $25 million federal/healthcare. EMEA 28% ($54 million, +35%) on NIS2/GDPR, Bechtle 50% SASE growth in DACH. APAC 17% ($33 million, +42%), NTT Data Japan $12 million cloud wins, CtrlS India on RBI rules.

Enablement via Partner Portal 2.0: sandboxes for GenAI deception, demos for CSPM; 4,500 certified, 65% Elite. Hyperscaler co-sell: 30% via AWS/Azure MP, 40% cycle cuts, 55% consumption pricing. Integrations with Falcon/SentinelOne for EDR-XDR. MDR program with 50 MSPs for SOCaaS, $50 million ARR by FY25.

Channels to hit 65% FY24 revenue, partner ARR $420 million TTM +30% YoY, 118% channel NRR. 90-day $120 million inventory buffers APAC risks. $15 million FY25 for PQC sandboxes.

Channels are our moat in $215 billion TAM, 70% partner-flow.

Turning to customers with ARR over $100K, a marker of deep ties. Q3 closed with 458 such customers, +37% YoY from 334, +8% sequential from 424. They drive 68% total ARR, up from 62%.

YTD 124 net adds, NRR 118% from CWPP/MDR upsells, akin to CrowdStrike's 115%+.

Enterprises (5,000+ endpoints) 72% or 330, +42% YoY, strong in finance/healthcare post-ransomware. Mid-market 128, +28%, via AWS/Azure Marketplace for Kubernetes security.

NA 65% (298, +32%) on CMMC/EO 14028. EMEA +52% to 92 on NIS2/DORA, two Tier-1 banks to full Zero Trust. APAC +61% to 54, Sydney DC for XDR vs. APT41/Lazarus. LatAm 14, +50% on LGPD.

Tech drivers: Nexus 4.0 GenAI SIEM cuts MTTR 45%, 67 Q3 expansions. SOAR integrations, ML on 10T events beat AV. $1.2M avg ARR/customer +12% YoY in $188B market +14%.

FY25 guide 550-600, 20-30% growth, $250M sales ramp, 3.2x pipeline, 95% retention vs. threats.

Before guidance details, non-GAAP FY25 revenue $1.25B-$1.28B, 28-31% growth midpoint; ARR +32-35%; op margins 26-28%.

Assumptions: 14.4% CAGR cybersecurity to $215B on 37% ransomware, cloud +25%, 78% LLM deploys needing ASPM; 45% EDR alerts from AI phishing. No deep recession, cyber table stakes 92%, 2-3% headwind offset.

1,200 net adds, 60% large enterprise, NRR 118-122%, 15% ACV expansion to SASE/ZTA; Nexus XDR 40% new ARR via Azure/AWS ties; pricing +4-5%, churn <4%, 98% gross retention.

GTM: 20% sales ramp on $150M AI tools, 85% utilization; channels 55% bookings via Accenture/Deloitte, Palo/CrowdStrike co-sell.

Regions: NA 65% rev +30% federal/commercial; EMEA +35% NIS2/EU Cloud ID vs. Zscaler/Netskope; APAC +45% Tokyo DC/NTT/Tata, China stable; LatAm +25% FX hedge.

Margins: 82-84% gross +200bps ASIC efficiencies vs. 5% chip inflation; OpEx 55% rev -300bps, 15% headcount R&D $220M quantum/GenAI; FCF 28-30% post $100M SBC/$50M M&A like supply chain buy.

Risks hedged: 95% retention, no reg shocks (SEC rules boost disclosure), TSMC/Samsung sourcing. Upside: SASE surge or outages +2-3pts growth.

Stress-tested vs. IDC/Forrester; conservative yet poised to outperform.

Next, Lisa Chen will provide more technical details.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing our NeuroThreat engine for behavioral analytics, rolling out ShieldGenAI for adversary emulation, and pioneering post-quantum cryptography to counter future crypto threats, all integrated into our Unified Threat Fabric for seamless EDR, NDR, and CWPP convergence.

Raj Patel: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, from FedRAMP High and CMMC readiness to GDPR/EBA data sovereignty and NIST-compliant quantum resistance.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session. At this time, please press star one if you have a question. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Mike, can you expand on the competitive dynamics in XDR and how win rates are translating to share gains?

Mike Harlan: Thanks, John. Absolutely, as I detailed earlier, our 51% XDR win rates are directly fueling those 3.6-point share jumps, particularly through lower false positives and faster MTTR. Customers are consolidating to platforms like ShieldXDR, and we're seeing that in multi-product deals averaging 3.2 modules. Happy to dive deeper if needed.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Great, thanks. Mike, on guidance assumptions, how sensitive is the outlook to APAC stabilization or channel ramp?

Mike Harlan: Emily, good question. We've baked in conservative APAC growth with China offsets from Japan/India, and channels at 55-65% bookings with strong inventory buffers. Overall, the model holds with 2-3% macro headwinds, but upside from threats or SASE adoption could add points. Details in my earlier assumptions walkthrough.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Gupta with Barclays.

Raj Gupta: Thanks. Lisa, technically, how is the NeuroThreat engine performing in MITRE evals, and any updates on GenAI integrations?

Lisa Chen: Raj, NeuroThreat delivered 45% lower false positives in latest MITRE, powering our mid-market strength. On GenAI, ShieldGenAI beta is live for 500 users, integrating with LangChain to block prompt injections, reducing analyst burnout by 35% in pilots—core to our R&D push.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan.

Lisa Wong: Congrats team. Sarah, on high-value customers, what's driving the 118% NRR there, and FY25 path to 550-600?

Sarah Kline: Thanks, Lisa. That NRR stems from seamless expansions into CWPP and MDR, Nexus 4.0 cutting MTTR 45%, and sticky integrations lowering switch costs. With $250 million sales investment and 3.2x pipeline, we're on track for that FY25 cohort growth, anchored by enterprise verticals and global ramps.

Sarah Kline: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
